title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 200 (Central Government or company to fix limit with regard to remuneration)

content.overview: Section 200 provides that notwithstanding anything contained in this Chapter, the Central Government or a company may, while according its approval under section 196 to any appointment or to any remuneration under section 197 in respect of any cases where the company has inadequate or no profits, fix the remuneration within the limits specified in this Act, at such amount or percentage of profits of the company, as it may deem fit. While fixing such remuneration, regard shall be had to the financial position of the company, the remuneration or commission drawn by the person concerned in any other capacity, the remuneration or commission drawn by him from any other company, professional qualifications and experience of the person concerned, and other matters as may be prescribed.
content.glance: When CG or the company approves appointment (s. 196) or remuneration (s. 197) in no/inadequate-profit cases, it may fix the amount or percentage within Act limits, having regard to financial position, other remuneration drawn, professional qualifications/experience, and prescribed factors.
content.study: Notwithstanding anything contained in this Chapter, the Central Government or a company may, while according its approval under section 196, to any appointment or to any remuneration under section 197, in respect of cases where the company has inadequate or no profits, fix the remuneration within the limits specified in this Act, at such amount or percentage of profits of the company, as it may deem fit and while fixing the remuneration, regard shall be had to—(a) the financial position of the company; (b) the remuneration or commission drawn by the individual concerned in any other capacity; (c) the remuneration or commission drawn by him from any other company; (d) professional qualifications and experience of the individual concerned; (e) such other matters as may be prescribed. Current-law framing: identify a no/inadequate-profit appointment or remuneration approval under ss. 196–197; apply the factors in s. 200 when fixing the amount or percentage within Act limits. The operative percentage ceilings remain in s. 197 read with Schedule V; s. 200 directs how the approving authority exercises its fixing power.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body: Applies when the Central Government or a company accords approval under s. 196 (appointment) or s. 197 (remuneration) in cases of inadequate or no profits.

sections.heading: Fixing Power
sections.body: Remuneration may be fixed within the limits in the Act, at such amount or percentage of profits as the authority deems fit.

sections.heading: Mandatory Factors
sections.body: Financial position of the company; remuneration/commission in any other capacity; remuneration/commission from any other company; professional qualifications and experience; other prescribed matters.

provisions.title: Central Government or company to fix limit with regard to remuneration

examples.title: Inadequate profits — CG factors
examples.body: A public company with inadequate profits seeks approval for MD remuneration under the Schedule V / s. 197 path. When fixing the amount, the approving authority must have regard to the company’s financial position, other remuneration the MD draws, and his professional qualifications under s. 200.

examples.title: Not a free-standing package right
examples.body: A proposed MD argues that s. 200 entitles him to a particular package. Section 200 does not create a right to a package; it directs the factors the approving authority must consider when fixing remuneration within Act limits.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 200 replace the 11% ceiling in s. 197?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 200 operates within the limits specified in the Act. The overall and individual ceilings in s. 197 (and Schedule V where applicable) remain the outer frame; s. 200 guides how the amount is fixed inside that frame in no/inadequate-profit approval cases.

distinctions.title: Fixing factors (s. 200) vs remuneration ceilings (s. 197)
distinctions.left: How the approving authority weighs factors when fixing pay in no/inadequate-profit cases
distinctions.right: Quantitative overall and individual percentage ceilings

misconceptions.trap: Section 200 is a free-standing power to pay any managerial package the Central Government likes.
misconceptions.correction: Section 200 applies when approving appointment or remuneration under ss. 196–197 in no/inadequate-profit cases, and the amount must still be within the limits specified in the Act, having regard to the listed factors.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 200 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm no/inadequate-profit approval under ss. 196–197. II. Identify the fixing authority. III. Apply the mandatory factors. IV. Stay within Act limits. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Approval context; factors applied; limits; precise relief.

examTips: Factors for fixing in no/inadequate-profit cases.
Within Act limits — does not override s. 197 ceilings.

enhancement.definition: Section 200 directs the Central Government or a company, when approving appointment or remuneration under ss. 196–197 in no/inadequate-profit cases, to fix the amount within Act limits having regard to financial position, other remuneration, qualifications and prescribed factors.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Managerial pay in loss or low-profit companies is fixed by reference to objective factors, not by unconstrained discretion.
essentialIngredients: Approval under s. 196 or s. 197 in no/inadequate-profit cases

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 200 is a direction to the approving authority, not a free-standing entitlement to any package.
